turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_target_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_target_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have a yield strength CLOSEST to 1051 MPa — not the highest, the closest to that value — then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".


The data files for this task are in your current working directory:
  - alloy_pair_target_train.csv
  - alloy_pair_target_pool.csv
Read them from disk. Give your answer as your final message — do not write it to a file.
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis

**Training data (n=300):** yield strength ranges 140–909 MPa (mean 468, max 909). The requested 1051 MPa is **above the entire observed range**, so "closest to 1051" reduces to "highest predicted strength" — with a preference for candidates that models agree are at the extreme top.

**Signals in the data:**
- `heat_treatment = quench_temper` is the strongest processing lever (mean 573 MPa vs 346 annealed); `route = wrought` > cast > AM (516 / 467 / 407).
- Strength rises with C, Mo, V, Ni, Co (precipitation + solid-solution hardening), with low aging_temp (~520–560 °C tempering) and long aging_time; Fe-rich/dilute compositions are weak.
- Relationships are clearly non-linear (RBF-SVR/GP beat linear models markedly).

**Modelling:** 9-model library (RBF-SVR ×2, GBM, HistGBM, RF, ExtraTrees, poly-2 Lasso/Ridge, anisotropic-RBF GP) stacked with NNLS weights on out-of-fold predictions, averaged over 8 CV seeds.
- Best singles: SVR R²≈0.85 (MAE 34), GBM 0.82, poly-Lasso 0.81
- **Stacked ensemble: R² ≈ 0.857, MAE ≈ 31 MPa** (weights dominated by SVR ≈0.45, GP ≈0.24, GBM ≈0.11, Lasso² ≈0.11)

**Top predictions (MPa, ±seed SD):**

| id | pred | sd |
|---|---|---|
| c060 | 838 | 8 |
| c082 | 837 | 8 |
| c099 | 834 | 8 |
| c049 | 831 | 10 |
| c069 | 830 | 9 |
| c052 | 826 | 8 |
| c085 | 809 | 8 |
| c017 | 803 | 10 |

The leading cluster is chemically coherent and exactly what the training data says is strongest: **quench_temper + wrought**, medium-high C (0.42–0.70), Ni 7.6–12.7, Mo ~1.9–2.3, V ~0.5–0.65, Co-bearing, low tempering temp (525–590 °C), long aging (~30–37 h), solutionizing ~1125–1160 °C. These same six rank top in the standalone SVR, GP and rank-vote ensembles, so the selection is robust across model families. (c017/c094 top the plain rank-vote but sit lower in the accuracy-weighted stack; they are leaner alloys and are kept as backups.)

**Final: c060, c082, c099, c049, c069**

**Training data (n=300):** yield strength ranges 140–909 MPa (mean 468, max 909). The requested 1051 MPa is **above the entire observed range**, so "closest to 1051" reduces to "highest predicted strength" — with a preference for candidates that models agree are at the extreme top.

**Signals in the data:**
- `heat_treatment = quench_temper` is the strongest processing lever (mean 573 MPa vs 346 annealed); `route = wrought` > cast > AM (516 / 467 / 407).
